candidate.educational_objective: Identify reduction or delay of skeletal-related complications as a major therapeutic purpose of zoledronic acid used with standard antineoplastic therapy for bone metastases.

options.A: Reduce skeletal-related events such as pathologic fracture, radiation or surgery to bone, and spinal cord compression.
options.B: Replace antineoplastic therapy by directly eradicating the client's underlying solid tumor.
options.C: Increase bone resorption so metastatic lesions release less calcium into the bloodstream.
options.D: Prevent every episode of cancer-related bone pain regardless of tumor progression or other causes.

candidate.rationale: Zoledronic acid is a bisphosphonate indicated for patients with documented bone metastases from solid tumors in conjunction with standard antineoplastic therapy. In the oncology clinical trials, skeletal-related events included pathologic fracture, radiation therapy to bone, surgery to bone, and spinal cord compression. Zoledronic acid does not replace treatment of the underlying malignancy, does not increase bone resorption, and the prescribing information does not support a guarantee that all cancer-related bone pain will be prevented.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Zoledronic acid is indicated with standard antineoplastic therapy for documented bone metastases from solid tumors. Oncology trials evaluated skeletal-related events including pathologic fracture, radiation therapy to bone, surgery to bone, and spinal cord compression, and demonstrated effects on these outcomes in studied populations.
